doc.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013

title: Opening and the myth of practicing at 5 a.m.
summary: Monk Rowe introduces Johnstone; they joke about a student's claim that he practices three hours every dawn, which he denies.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I’m in Fredonia, New York, actually we’re in Dunkirk, but we’re both here because of Fredonia sort of. And I’m happy to have Bruce Johnstone here, baritone sax extraordinaire and composer and arranger.
It’s been a long way from New Zealand.

I saw a thing — we were just talking about a little YouTube thing, and apparently one of your students made a comment under it, and he said about Bruce, “he gets up every day at 5 a.m. and practices for three hours.” I’d like to see you do that. I’d like to see you do that. Now, is that true?
No it’s not. No it’s not.
But I do practice a lot, but I think they’re building a myth, which is fine if they want to do that. But obviously they must have some idle time that they need to be more deeply involved in.
